items.title: Weighted coefficient spaces form a Hilbert scale
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $H_0$ be a separable real Hilbert space with a complete orthonormal basis indexed by the disjoint union of a finite set $I_*$ and the level indices $(\ell,k)$ with $\ell\ge0$ and $0\le k<2^\ell$. Write the basis vectors as $(e_i)_{i\in I_*}$ and $(e_{\ell k})$. For $r\ge0$, define
$$H_r:=\left\{x\in H_0:\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle x,e_i\rangle_{H_0}|^2+\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{2r\ell}\sum_{k<2^\ell}|\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle_{H_0}|^2<\infty\right\},$$
with inner product given by the corresponding weighted coefficient sum and norm squared
$$\|x\|_{H_r}^2:=\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle x,e_i\rangle_{H_0}|^2+\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{2r\ell}\sum_{k<2^\ell}|\langle x,e_{\ell k}\rangle_{H_0}|^2.$$
Then $H_r$ is a separable real Hilbert space. Its displayed basis is complete and orthogonal in $H_r$, with squared basis norms $1$ on the finite family and $2^{2r\ell}$ on level $\ell$, and the inclusion $H_r\hookrightarrow H_0$ is continuous with operator norm at most $1$.
items.axiom_use: Countable choice is assumed only through the published square-summable orthogonal-series and Parseval results used to identify coefficient norms and reconstruct vectors from their coordinates.

items.title: Coordinate vectors form the Hilbert basis of real ell-two
items.statement: Let $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ with its canonical real inner product, and for each $j\in\mathbb N$ let $e_j$ be the sequence whose $j$th coordinate is $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. Then $(e_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal basis of $H$. For every $x=(x_j)\in H$, the truncations $\sum_{j=1}^N x_je_j$ converge in $H$ to $x$, and $\|x\|_2^2=\sum_{j\in\mathbb N}|x_j|^2$.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; coordinate truncations converge by the finite-tail property in the definition of square summability.

items.title: A Borel prior concentrated on a forward-map domain
items.statement: Let $X$ be a specified real separable Banach or Hilbert parameter space with metric $d_X(x,x')=\|x-x'\|_X$ and its norm topology. Let $(Y,d_Y)$ be a metric data space equipped with a sigma-algebra $\Sigma_Y$, let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty admissible truth set, and let $F:U\to Y$ be a forward map. Choose a Borel set $D\in\mathcal B(X)$ with $D\subseteq U$ such that the restriction $G:=F|_D:D\to Y$ is measurable for the trace Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(D):=\{D\cap A:A\in\mathcal B(X)\}$. A prior on this forward domain is a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ such that $\mu(D)=1$. Its restriction $\mu|_D$, defined by $\mu|_D(A)=\mu(A)$ for $A\in\mathcal B(D)$, is then a probability measure on $D$, and the induced data law is $G_\#(\mu|_D)$, defined by $G_\#(\mu|_D)(E)=(\mu|_D)(G^{-1}(E))$ for $E\in\Sigma_Y$. A Borel probability on $X$ with $\mu(D)<1$ is not a prior on this declared forward domain.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §1.3, equation (1.8), parameter domain X'⊆X on which G is defined; §3.2, prior on a separable Banach parameter space.

items.title: Weighted Hilbert Gaussian series and prior regularity
items.statement:
Let $H_0$ and $H_1$ be separable real Hilbert spaces with a continuous inclusion $H_1\hookrightarrow H_0$. Let $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $H_0$ that is a complete orthogonal basis of $H_1$, write $w_j=\|e_j\|_{H_1}^2>0$, and set $f_j=e_j/\sqrt{w_j}$, so $(f_j)_{j\ge1}$ is an orthonormal basis of $H_1$. Let $(\xi_j)_{j\ge1}$ be independent real random variables on one probability space with $\mathbb E\xi_j=0$ and $\mathbb E\xi_j^2=1$, and let $\lambda_j\ge0$ satisfy $\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_jw_j<\infty$. Then
$$S_N=\sum_{j=1}^N\sqrt{\lambda_j}\,\xi_j e_j$$
converges almost surely in $H_1$ and in $L^2(\Omega;H_1)$ to an $H_1$-valued Borel-measurable random element $S$, with
$$\mathbb E\|S\|_{H_1}^2=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_jw_j.$$
These norm-convergence conclusions use no choice axiom beyond the supplied probability space and variables. For the following Gaussian conclusions, assume in addition that each $\xi_j$ has the standard normal law $N(0,1)$. Under the Axiom of Choice and countable choice, $S$ is a centered Borel Gaussian random element in $H_1$. Its covariance map $C:H_1^*\to H_1$, transported to $H_1$ by the Hilbert-space Riesz identification, is diagonal in the basis $(f_j)_{j\ge1}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_jw_j$, and these eigenvalues are summable. If $D$ is a Borel forward-map domain in $H_1$ and $\mathbb P(S\in D)=1$, then the law of $S$ is a prior on $D$. Under the Axiom of Choice there is $a>0$ such that
$$\mathbb E\exp\!\bigl(a\|S\|_{H_1}^2\bigr)<\infty.$$
items.axiom_use: The almost-sure and L² convergence proof is choice-free once the probability space and independent centered unit-variance variables are supplied. Countable choice is used through the published square-summable scalar Gaussian-series law and Hilbert-space Riesz representation for the Gaussian and covariance branches. The library's Borel Gaussian, covariance, and Fernique interfaces require AC; Fernique is used only for the exponential-moment conclusion.

items.title: A Gaussian coefficient prior that misses uniform ellipticity
items.axiom_use: AC is required by the library's standard-normal law definition; the positive-mass and full-measure failure calculation itself is choice-free.
items.statement: Assume AC. Let parameter and data spaces be $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with their Borel sigma-algebras, let the admissible truth set be $U=\mathbb R$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be the identity map. Regard $\theta\in\mathbb R$ as the constant coefficient field $a_\theta(x)=\theta$ on $[0,1]$. Let $D=[1,2]\subseteq U$ be the uniformly elliptic class with lower bound $1$ and upper bound $2$, meaning $1\le a_\theta(x)\le2$ for every $x\in[0,1]$; the restricted map $G=F|_D$ is measurable. Give $X$ the standard normal law $\mu=N(0,1)$. Since $\mu((-\infty,1))>0$, $\mu(D)<1$; consequently $\mu$ is a Gaussian probability on the parameter space but is not a prior on this forward-map domain.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §1.3, positivity constraint and restricted forward-map domain; §3.4, elliptic inverse problem with a prior.

items.title: A trace-class Gaussian with full support and a proper Cameron–Martin space
items.axiom_use: AC and countable choice are assumed for the Gaussian-series law, covariance/RKHS construction, tightness, and support theorem. The coordinate-basis and weighted RKHS calculations use no further choice.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice. In $H=\ell^2$, define $e_j$ to be the sequence with value $1$ at coordinate $j$ and $0$ at every other coordinate. Let $\xi_j$ be independent $N(0,1)$ variables and set
$$W=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-1}\xi_j e_j.$$
Take the parameter and data spaces both to be $H$ with their Borel sigma-algebras, the admissible truth set and forward domain to be $U=D=H$, and the forward map to be the identity. The law $\mu$ of $W$ is a centered Borel Gaussian prior on $D$. Its covariance is diagonal with positive eigenvalues $j^{-2}$, whose finite sum $\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}$ makes it trace class, meaning that the sum of these nonnegative eigenvalues is finite. Its covariance reproducing-kernel Hilbert space is the dense proper subspace of $H$
$$\left\{x\in\ell^2:\sum_{j\ge1}j^2x_j^2<\infty\right\},$$
which is not all of $H$. The topological support of $\mu$, defined as the set of points every open neighborhood of which has positive $\mu$-measure, is all of $H$.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §2.4, Theorem 2.4, Remarks 2.5, and the Karhunen–Loève covariance convention.

items.title: A Gaussian wavelet series at the Besov threshold
items.axiom_use: AC is required by the library's standard-normal and Borel Gaussian interfaces. Countable choice is used through the L² and weighted-coefficient Hilbert-space results, the Gaussian-series law, and Borel measurability of the square map. The IID strong-law threshold divergence uses no further choice.
items.statement:
Assume AC and countable choice. Fix $s>0$ and a periodic $S$-regular orthonormal wavelet basis of $L^2([0,1])$ consisting of a finite family of coarsest scaling functions $(\varphi_i)_{i\in I_*}$ and detail wavelets $(\psi_{\ell k})_{\ell\ge0,\,0\le k<2^\ell}$, where $I_*$ is finite and $S>s$. Let $\xi_i$ and $\xi_{\ell k}$, over all these indices, be independent $N(0,1)$ variables. For $0\le r\le s$, define $B^r_{2,2}([0,1])$ to be the set of $f\in L^2([0,1])$ with finite coefficient norm
$$\|f\|_{B^r_{2,2}}^2=\sum_{i\in I_*}|\langle f,\varphi_i\rangle|^2+\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{2\ell r}\sum_{k<2^\ell}|\langle f,\psi_{\ell k}\rangle|^2.$$
Take parameter and data spaces $X=Y=L^2([0,1])$ with their Borel sigma-algebras, the admissible truth set and forward domain $U=D=X$, and the forward map $F=\mathrm{id}_X$. Set the coarsest scaling coefficients to zero and define
$$W=\sum_{\ell\ge0}\sum_{k<2^\ell}2^{-\ell(s+1/2)}\xi_{\ell k}\psi_{\ell k}.$$
The law of $W$ is a centered Borel Gaussian prior on $D$. For each fixed $0\le r<s$, $W$ belongs to $B^r_{2,2}([0,1])$ almost surely, but $W$ does not belong to the threshold space $B^s_{2,2}([0,1])$ almost surely.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §2.3, Theorem 2.2 and complete proof of Besov-prior regularity threshold; §2.4, Gaussian series convergence.
